title: Validate Binary Search Tree
contract: Use strict BST ordering: every left descendant < node < every right descendant; duplicates are invalid.
optimal: Tree root=tree(input);Deque<Tree> stack=new ArrayDeque<>();Tree node=root;Long previous=null;while(node!=null||!stack.isEmpty()){while(node!=null){stack.push(node);node=node.left;}node=stack.pop();emit("Inorder values must be strictly increasing","value",node.value,"previous",previous);if(previous!=null&&node.value<=previous)return false;previous=(long)node.value;node=node.right;}return true;
reasoning: The baseline checks every descendant against each ancestor, then recursively validates each subtree.
Inorder traversal of a valid strict BST is strictly increasing.
Keep the previous value, not a magic minimum sentinel, so Integer.MIN_VALUE is accepted as a real first value. Checking only immediate children misses ancestor violations.
